concepts.name: Leap years
concepts.description: A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except century years, which must be divisible by 400.

concepts.name: Odd days
concepts.description: The days left over after removing whole weeks decide how the weekday shifts.

concepts.name: Centuries
concepts.description: 100 years carry 5 odd days, 200 carry 3, 300 carry 1 and 400 carry 0.

concepts.name: Finding the day of the week
concepts.description: Count odd days from a known reference date to the target date.

concepts.name: Counting weekdays in a month
concepts.description: A 31-day month has 4 full weeks plus 3 extra days; those 3 weekdays occur five times.

formulas.title: Leap-year rule
formulas.prompt: When is a year a leap year?
formulas.formula:
Divisible by 4 → leap
Century years (ending 00) → leap only if divisible by 400
formulas.explanation: The Gregorian rule keeps the calendar aligned with the seasons. 1900 and 2100 are not leap years; 2000 and 2400 are.
formulas.commonMistake: Calling every century year a leap year.

formulas.title: Odd days
formulas.prompt: How many odd days does a year carry?
formulas.formula:
Odd days = (number of days) mod 7
Ordinary year: 365 = 52 weeks + 1 → 1 odd day
Leap year: 366 → 2 odd days
formulas.explanation: Only the days left after complete weeks change the weekday.
formulas.example: 1 Jan 2023 was Sunday → 1 Jan 2024 is Monday (2023 is ordinary).
formulas.commonMistake: Counting the total days instead of the remainder.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many odd days are in 3 ordinary years and one leap year?

formulas.title: Century odd days
formulas.prompt: How many odd days do 100, 200, 300 and 400 years contain?
formulas.formula:
100 years → 5 odd days
200 years → 3 odd days
300 years → 1 odd day
400 years → 0 odd days
formulas.explanation: 100 years have 24 leap years: 100 + 24 = 124 days = 17 weeks + 5. Doubling and tripling gives 3 and 1; 400 years have one more leap day and total 0.
formulas.commonMistake: Assuming every century has 24 leap years (400 years have 97).
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many odd days are there in 200 years?

formulas.title: Weekday of a date
formulas.prompt: How do you find the weekday of a date from a known one?
formulas.formula:
Days between the dates mod 7 = shift in weekday
0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, … 6 = Saturday
formulas.explanation: Add the odd days between the two dates to the known weekday. Remember a Feb 29 only counts if it lies between the dates.
formulas.example: 26 Jan 1950 was Thursday; 10 years and 2 leap days later: 12 mod 7 = 5 → Tuesday
formulas.commonMistake: Counting a leap day that falls before the starting date or after the target.
formulas.applicationPrompt: 26 January 1950 was a Thursday. What day was 26 January 1960?

formulas.title: Weekdays in a month
formulas.prompt: A month has 31 days and starts on a Wednesday. Which weekdays occur five times?
formulas.formula:
28 days = 4 full weeks
31 days → 3 extra days: the first 3 weekdays occur 5 times
30 days → first 2; 29 days → first 1
formulas.explanation: Every weekday appears four times in 28 days. The remaining days repeat the weekdays the month starts with.
formulas.example: 31 days from Wednesday: Wednesday, Thursday and Friday occur 5 times
formulas.commonMistake: Assuming the last weekdays are the repeated ones.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A 31-day month starts on a Wednesday. Which days occur only four times?

formulas.title: Same date, next year
formulas.prompt: On what weekday does the same date fall a year later?
formulas.formula: One weekday later, or two if 29 February falls in between
formulas.explanation: A year of 365 days is 52 weeks and 1 day; a leap day adds one more.
formulas.example: 15 August 2023 was a Tuesday. 29 February 2024 lies in between, so 15 August 2024 was a Thursday.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding two days just because one of the years is a leap year, without checking that 29 February is actually crossed.
formulas.applicationPrompt: 1 January 2025 was a Wednesday. What day was 1 January 2026?

levels.title: Leftover Days Decide the Weekday
levels.description: Remove whole weeks and only the odd days matter.

blocks.title: Only the remainder matters
blocks.body: A week has 7 days, so after any whole number of weeks the weekday is unchanged. An ordinary year has 365 = 52 × 7 + 1 days: one odd day. A leap year has two.

blocks.title: Leap years and centuries
blocks.body:
Leap: divisible by 4 (centuries: by 400)
100 years → 5 odd days
200 → 3, 300 → 1, 400 → 0
blocks.caption: 1900 and 2100 are not leap years; 2000 is.

blocks.title: Counting to a date
blocks.body: To find a weekday, add up the odd days from a known reference to the target date, reduce by 7 and step forward from the known weekday. Only count a 29 February if it lies between the two dates.

levels.title: Calendars Formulas
levels.description: Leap years, odd days, centuries, weekdays and month counts.

levels.title: From a Known Date
levels.description: Shift the weekday and count within a month.

questions.question: Which of these is a leap year?
questions.explanation: 1900 and 2100 are century years not divisible by 400, so they are not leap years. 2022 is not divisible by 4. 2000 is divisible by 400, so it is a leap year.

hints.text: Century years follow a stricter rule.

questions.question: How many odd days does an ordinary (non-leap) year contain?
questions.explanation: 365 = 52 × 7 + 1, so an ordinary year has 1 odd day.

hints.text: How many days are left after 52 complete weeks?

commonMistakes: Answering 2, which is a leap year.

questions.question: How many odd days are there in 100 years?
questions.explanation: 100 years contain 24 leap years, so 24 × 366 + 76 × 365 = 36,524 days = 5217 weeks + 5 days. Equivalently 100 + 24 = 124 = 17 weeks + 5 odd days.
questions.method: Ordinary years give 1, leap years give 2.

hints.text: 100 years have 24 leap years (the century year is ordinary).

questions.question: A century year (such as 1700 or 2000) is a leap year only if it is divisible by
questions.explanation: Century years must be divisible by 400. That is why 2000 is a leap year but 1900 is not.

hints.text: 1900 is divisible by 4 and 100, but is it a leap year?

questions.question: 1 January 2023 was a Sunday. What day was 1 January 2024?
questions.explanation: 2023 is an ordinary year with 1 odd day, so the weekday shifts by one: Sunday → Monday.
commonMistakes: Shifting by 2 as if it were a leap year.

questions.question: 26 January 1950 was a Thursday. What day of the week was 26 January 1960?
questions.explanation: 10 years pass. The leap days in between are 29 February 1952 and 29 February 1956 (1960's comes after 26 January), so 10 + 2 = 12 odd days = 5 after removing a week. Thursday + 5 = Tuesday.
questions.method: Count only leap days between the two dates.
commonMistakes: Counting 1960 as a leap day too (which gives Wednesday).

questions.question: How many odd days are there from 1 January 2001 to 31 December 2004 (both dates included)?
questions.explanation: 2001, 2002 and 2003 are ordinary (1 odd day each = 3), and 2004 is a leap year (2 odd days). Total = 5 odd days.

hints.text: Which of the four years is a leap year?

commonMistakes: Counting all four years as 1 odd day (4).

questions.question: What day of the week was 15 August 1947?
questions.explanation: Odd days: 1600 years → 0; 300 years (1601–1900) → 1; 46 years (1901–1946) with 11 leap years → 57 mod 7 = 1; 15 August 1947 is day 227 of the year → 227 mod 7 = 3. Total 0 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 5 → Friday.
questions.method: Centuries, then whole years, then days in the year.

hints.text: Count the days from 1 January to 15 August.

commonMistakes: Counting 12 leap years, or starting the days count at 0.

questions.question: A month has 31 days and begins on a Wednesday. Which of these days occurs only four times in that month?
questions.explanation: 31 = 4 weeks + 3 days. The first three weekdays of the month (Wednesday, Thursday, Friday) occur five times; every other day, including Saturday, occurs four times.
solutionSteps: They repeat the first 3 weekdays: Wed, Thu, Fri.
questions.method: The extra days repeat the starting weekdays.

hints.text: How many days are left after four full weeks?

questions.question: How many odd days are there in 200 years?
questions.explanation: 100 years carry 5 odd days, so 200 years carry 10 = 3 after removing a week.
questions.method: Double the century figure and reduce mod 7.

hints.text: Start with the 5 odd days in 100 years.

questions.question: What day of the week was 1 January 2000?
questions.explanation: Up to 31 December 1999: 1600 years → 0; 300 years → 1; 99 years (1901–1999) with 24 leap years → 99 + 24 = 123 → 4. Total 5 → Friday. So 1 January 2000 was a Saturday.
questions.method: Count odd days up to the day before, then add one.

hints.text: Find the weekday of 31 December 1999 first.

questions.question: What day of the week was 1 January 1901?
questions.explanation: Up to 31 December 1900: 1600 years → 0 and 300 years → 1, so 31 December 1900 was a Monday. Then 1 January 1901 was a Tuesday.
questions.method: Centuries reset the count; add the extra day.

questions.question: 5 March 2024 was a Tuesday. What day of the week is 5 March 2027?
questions.explanation: From 5 March 2024 to 5 March 2027 is 3 years. 29 February 2024 has already passed and 29 February 2028 is after the target, so no leap day lies between: 3 odd days. Tuesday + 3 = Friday.
solutionSteps: No leap day between the dates.
questions.method: Count leap days only between the two dates.
commonMistakes: Adding a leap day for 2024 or 2028.
